title: Skeleton: who stands behind NEAR's validators?
question: who stands behind NEAR's validators?
note: Hand-made (T020), in the tool order of quickstart step 2: get_snapshot, describe_snapshot, compute_figures, propose_spec with segments backers, validate_spec with the interpretation, render_flower, then the answer. {"$from": "<call id>.<path>"} takes a value from an earlier tool result in the conversation; {{<call id>.<path>}} puts one into text. Numbers in the answer come only from tool results.

interpretation.summary: Stake decides who produces NEAR's blocks. {{call_3.nakamoto.count}} of the {{call_3.participants_included}} seated validators together hold more than a third of it, enough to stall the chain. Behind each pool stand its backers: many small delegators, a few large accounts, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.

power_means.claim: A validator's power is its stake in the current epoch: it sets how many blocks and chunks the validator produces.
{{call_3.nakamoto.count}} validators together pass the one-third threshold that BFT consensus needs to halt.
Stake is lent to a pool by its delegators; they can move it, so they share the pool's power.

mappings.why: Share of stake is the power that counts here, compressed into a band so small validators stay visible.
Bar height repeats the share, on a square-root scale, so the largest validators stand out.
Kind of account tells pools from liquid-staking entities.
Pool names are self-declared on-chain, so they are drawn as self-declared, never verified.
Each bar is cut into the backers of the pool: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.
Largest first, clockwise from the top, so the validators that matter most are read first.

conflicts: House of Stake voting power (veNEAR) is a second kind of power on NEAR; this flower draws block-production stake only.
unknowns: Who controls the large implicit (hex) delegators: most of the biggest delegators have no public name.
Who owns the lockup contracts: their owners were not resolved.
Whether several pools are run by one operator: pools are not merged without evidence.
inferred: A named .near account is a self-declared name, not a verified identity.

turns.content: Here is the flower of NEAR's validators, from a stored snapshot of block {{call_1.snapshot.block_height}}. {{call_3.nakamoto.count}} of {{call_3.participants_included}} seated validators together hold more than a third of the stake (the Nakamoto coefficient). Each bar is cut into the pool's backers: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups. What the data can't tell: who controls the large unnamed accounts, who owns the lockups, and whether several pools share one operator. Open it here: {{call_6.view_url}}
